memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'If anyone dedicates their house as something holy to the LORD, the
priest will judge its quality as good or bad. Whatever value the priest
then sets, so it will remain. If the one who dedicates the house wishes
to redeem it, they must add a fifth to its value, and the house will
again be theirs'" - Lev 27:14-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The vows now move from animals to a house — a person's home, one of the
most valuable and personal things they owned. A family could dedicate
even their house to the Lord.

Think about what that meant. To dedicate your house was to say, "Lord,
this place where I live, where my family eats and sleeps, is Yours. My
most private space belongs to You."

Dear friend, there is a beautiful challenge in this for us. Have we ever
dedicated our homes to God? Not the building itself as a religious ritual,
but the life lived inside it — the conversations, the welcome given at the
door, the way family members treat one another when no guests are
watching.

Joshua declared, as for me and my household, we will serve the LORD (Josh
24:15). The early church met in homes, and those ordinary houses became
places where the gospel spread and lives were changed (Acts 2:46; Rom
16:5).

Your home can be a small outpost of God's kingdom — a place of hospitality
where the lonely are welcomed, a place of peace in a stressful world, a
place where children first learn who Jesus is.

Dedicate your home to God today, not with a ceremony, but with a decision
about the kind of life that will be lived within its walls.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Whom does my home really serve — God, or my own comfort?
2. Is my home a place of welcome and peace, or of tension?
3. What would it look like to dedicate my household to the Lord?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, this home and the life lived inside it belong to You. Make it a
place of welcome, peace and love, where Your presence is known. Amen.
